description: We are Outer Space, a team of developers and creative minds from Zulia, Venezuela, collaborating remotely. United by our curiosity about the cosmos and a drive to solve NASA's challenges using open data, our Zulian spark fuels our determination to overcome any distance or technical hurdle, turning complex problems into real, out-of-this-world solutions.
summary:
Planet X y SPHEREx is a public web app that turns thousands of calibrated SPHEREx infrared images into something you can actually explore. You search for an object by name, preset or coordinates, and the app finds every available frame in NASA's IRSA archive (spherex_dr1 and spherex_qr3), then loads them into one viewer with time-lapse, blink and difference views, plus zoom, GIF export and shareable links.

The challenge is volume and complexity: six detector bands, many epochs, technical file names and cutouts in FITS. The app hides that behind one page with two modes. Casual mode is purely visual; Science mode adds a parallax distance from the nearest Gaia DR3 star (via the Heidelberg TAP service) and an aperture magnitude for each frame, plotted as a light curve.

It matters because it makes real infrared survey data explorable without downloading files or installing software, in Spanish or English, on phone or laptop. It is a visualization and exploration tool, not a detection of any object.
details:
What it does Planet X y SPHEREx is a single-page web app for exploring calibrated SPHEREx infrared images. The user enters a name (resolved via CDS Sesame / SIMBAD–NED), a preset, or coordinates. The server queries IRSA SIA v2 for the collections spherex_dr1 and spherex_qr3, returns up to 24 dates covering that position, and renders each cutout to PNG on the fly.

The viewer offers playback, blink, difference between two dates, zoom, GIF export and a shareable URL. A Casual / Science switch sets the depth: Science mode adds band and field-of-view controls, the nearest Gaia DR3 star within 29″ (parallax, RUWE, distance in pc and ly) and aperture photometry with a magnitude curve.

Benefits and impact No downloads, no Python, no FITS handling: real survey data in a browser, on phone or laptop, in Spanish or English. Useful for students, teachers and outreach, and open enough to serve as a teaching example of coordinates, epochs and photometry.

Tools Python 3.11+, FastAPI, Uvicorn, httpx, NumPy, Astropy, Pillow and matplotlib colormaps; plain HTML/CSS/JS embedded in the app with Tailwind CDN; deployed on FastAPI Cloud. No React, no Node, no database, no FITS written to disk. Data: NASA/IPAC IRSA, ESA Gaia DR3, CDS Sesame.

What is creative Cutouts stream only until the image extension arrives, so the heavy table extensions are never downloaded; when IRSA rejects a small box, the request widens and is cropped back locally. Caches in memory, state in the URL, one file with no build step.

What we considered Calibrated collections only (spherex_qr2 excluded), honesty about limits (field star, aperture magnitudes, no detection claims), reliability against IRSA 503s, and accessibility on mobile with a bilingual interface.
